note: Final vocabulary after the merge phase (r01-r04, 60 papers, 2109 nodes, 2625 edges). Three levels at most: L1 argument stage -> L2 group (OBS and STR only) -> leaf. Types name the ROLE in the argument; technique, material, quantity, direction, mechanism class and basis go in attrs. Every leaf carries definition, rule (decision vs nearest sibling), example and usage. See vocab/HIERARCHY.md and rounds/r04/judge.md.
design_principles: A distinction is a type only if it changes the next inference; everything else is an attribute (aspect, via, form, proxy, object, property_family).
Types name the role in the argument, never the technique or material; figure form (modality), data origin (provenance) and figure fidelity (image_support) are node fields, not types.

Keep the argument skeleton fixed (HYP -> DES -> PRC -> STR -> PRP -> PRF -> DSC, with OBS/KNW as evidence and premises and MEC as bridge) and absorb new cases with boundary rules before adding leaves.
Siblings are separated by a written decision rule a new annotator can apply; where staff could not apply it, the siblings were merged unless the next inference differs.
An entry used in fewer than 2 of 60 papers survives only if clearly general across material classes.
mm_ops name the figure act and its failure modes; what follows from the act is carried by the dst node type, not by the op name.

HYP.definition: Stage 1, why: the motivation, gap, need or testable expectation the work sets out from.

HYP/gap.definition: Something is unknown, unmeasured, unexplained or contradictory in the literature; closing it yields knowledge. attrs.gap_kind = unobserved_regime | unexplained_effect | conflicting_reports.
HYP/gap.rule: vs need: closing a gap yields KNOWLEDGE; closing a need yields a BETTER MATERIAL. If both are stated, type the one the conclusion answers.
HYP/gap.example: Kinetics of the alpha-to-beta transformation in Ti at ns time scales have never been measured directly

HYP/need.definition: An application or societal requirement (property level, cost, sustainability, safety) that current materials fail to meet.
HYP/need.rule: vs gap: see gap. vs hypothesis: a need states a shortfall, not what should fix it.
HYP/need.example: Mg alloy AZ91 lacks creep resistance above 150 C

HYP/hypothesis.definition: A testable expectation or proposed strategy: doing X should produce Y. The work later confirms, refutes or qualifies it.
HYP/hypothesis.rule: vs DES/*: the hypothesis states the expected effect; the DES node states the concrete choice that tests it.
HYP/hypothesis.example: Adding SiC particles should raise the strength and creep resistance of the Mg matrix

DES.definition: Stage 2, choice: a reasoned decision about material, geometry, route, method or comparison axis.

DES/base_system.definition: Choice of the host/base material or starting feedstock, with the reason (cost, renewability, known structure, availability). For a molecule designed as a whole (multi-domain peptide, chimera) with no identifiable host, the whole design is base_system.
DES/base_system.rule: vs modification: modification only when something is ADDED TO or SUBSTITUTED INTO a named base; no identifiable base -> base_system.
DES/base_system.example: Use non-edible karanja oil as the polyol feedstock; choose AZ91 as matrix

DES/modification.definition: Choice to add or substitute a constituent into a base (dopant, alloying element, reinforcement, filler, co-monomer, additive). Site, amount and intended role in attrs. Verification of incorporation follows.
DES/modification.rule: vs base_system: see base_system. vs variable_sweep: the constituent is the modification; its levels are the sweep.
DES/modification.example: Substitute Cr3+ on the Ti4+ site because the ionic radii match

DES/architecture.definition: A priori geometric or spatial target to be built: pore/channel lattice, external shape, strut network, layer stacking, core-shell, graded placement. Geometry source and dimensions in attrs. A design-fidelity check (match_to_design) follows.
DES/architecture.rule: vs route: architecture is WHAT geometry is targeted; route is HOW it is made.
DES/architecture.example: 8 mm cylinders with orthogonal 500-800 um channels at 50% designed pore volume

DES/route.definition: Choice of processing route, technique, schedule or auxiliary (solvent, catalyst, atmosphere) justified against a baseline or a structural target, including a schedule designed to isolate one process (attrs.purpose = decouple).
DES/route.rule: vs method: route decides how the material is MADE; method decides how it is MEASURED. A processing schedule that exists to isolate a process is still route (purpose=decouple), not method or sweep.
DES/route.example: Replace xylene with bio-derived dipentene; 180 C/5 h to finish recrystallisation before growth at 250 C

DES/method.definition: Choice of characterization/test method, specimen geometry or sampling protocol because it enables or validates a measurement. attrs.aspect = technique | specimen | sampling. Spine only when the method is a headline contribution; it then realizes the claim it makes measurable.
DES/method.example: Use single-shot dynamic TEM on 75 nm films, each shot on a fresh region

DES/variable_sweep.definition: The controlled variable(s) and levels that form the comparison axis of the study. Variable and levels in attrs.
DES/variable_sweep.rule: vs modification/route: the sweep node carries the LEVELS; what is varied is typed separately only if its choice is argued.
DES/variable_sweep.example: Reinforcement content 0-25 wt% in 5 wt% steps

DES/down_select.definition: A design decision made after, and because of, an observation, screen or weighed claim; reached by motivates from OBS/PRP/PRF/MEC. Screen-then-choose papers put it on the spine.
DES/down_select.rule: vs other DES: down_select has an incoming motivates edge from a RESULT of this paper; a priori choices are the other DES leaves.
DES/down_select.example: IPDI chosen as the diisocyanate after the coating-quality screen

PRC.definition: Stage 3, act: a processing act or exposure applied to make, shape, modify or probe the material.

PRC/synthesis.definition: A reaction or assembly step that turns precursors into the target compound, phase, polymer or colloidal object (solid-state reaction, sol-gel incl. calcination of the gel, co-precipitation, polymerisation, functionalisation, self-assembly in dispersion). Reactive consolidation (reactive HP/SPS, SHS) is ONE synthesis node with attrs.concurrent_forming=true.
PRC/synthesis.rule: vs treatment: if the input is not yet the target compound (precursor, gel, hydroxide, salt, mixed oxides) it is synthesis even when thermal; if it already is, treatment.
PRC/synthesis.example: Epoxidise oil C=C bonds with H2O2 over Amberlyst 15

PRC/forming.definition: Turning feedstock (powder, melt, solution, sol, pellets) into a bulk body or designed shape: casting, sintering/HP/SPS of the made compound, compaction, extrusion or moulding of feedstock, additive manufacturing, composite mixing-and-solidification, in-situ gelation, lithographic/subtractive patterning, direct writing, laser drilling, transfer printing.
PRC/forming.rule: vs treatment: forming turns FEEDSTOCK into a body; working an already-made solid body (rolling, forging, ECAP, hot extrusion of a cast billet) is treatment. vs deposition: onto a substrate as film/coating = deposition.
PRC/forming.example: Spark plasma sintering of powders into >96% dense pellets

PRC/deposition.definition: Applying material onto a substrate as film, coating or layer (PVD, CVD, spin/bar coating, electrodeposition, spraying, on-substrate self-assembly, in-situ cure of an applied coating), including chemical conversion coatings grown by reaction with the substrate (attrs.aspect = conversion).
PRC/deposition.rule: vs forming: the product sits on a substrate and substrate-coating properties follow -> deposition; a free-standing body -> forming.
PRC/deposition.example: Bar-coat 120 um films on steel panels; Sr-P conversion coating on Mg

PRC/joining.definition: Joining pre-made bodies into one assembly across a new interface: diffusion bonding, brazing, welding, TLP and adhesive bonding. Joint properties follow with attrs.object='joint'.
PRC/joining.rule: vs deposition: joining bonds two pre-made BODIES; deposition grows new material on one.
PRC/joining.example: Vacuum diffusion bonding of EHEA and TiAl blocks at 900-1000 C

PRC/treatment.definition: Modifying the structure of an already-made material of the target compound: annealing, ageing, solution treatment, quenching, curing of a made polymer, thermomechanical working, electropulsing, surface/irradiation treatment as part of making, milling/classification of a made powder. In computation papers, a pressure/strain applied to find the stable phase that is then kept (attrs.in_silico=true).
PRC/treatment.rule: vs stimulus: treatment makes the material to be USED; stimulus probes or tests the finished material. vs synthesis: see synthesis.
PRC/treatment.example: Solution treatment at 520 C then ageing at 180 C; wet milling of Si to d50 = 62 nm

PRC/stimulus.definition: An external perturbation or exposure (thermal pulse, load, field, bias or cycling, corrosive/biological environment, irradiation; in silico, a pressure applied to read a property) whose effect IS the object of study. Create a stimulus node only when the exposure produces an argued state (post-mortem STR, in-situ readout); a standard service test is carried by attrs.condition on the PRF node.
PRC/stimulus.rule: vs treatment: see treatment. vs PRF attrs.condition: no argued structural/response state from the exposure -> no stimulus node.
PRC/stimulus.example: Single 12 ns laser pulse heats the film at 1e11 K/s during pump-probe imaging

OBS.definition: Evidence: a readout from a measurement or computation before interpretation; never spine. Subtype names WHAT FEATURE of the data is read; modality, provenance and image_support are node fields.

OBS/signal.definition: Discrete features of a trace (peaks, bands, reflections, edges, steps, pole-figure maxima) read individually, or a whole trace judged against a reference or model trace.

OBS/signal/reference_match.definition: A whole measured trace (pattern, spectrum or response curve) judged to coincide or not with a reference trace: parent sample, standard, database card, or model/fit/simulation output (Rietveld, theory curve, constructed image).
OBS/signal/reference_match.rule: vs feature_assignment: WHOLE-trace coincidence -> reference_match; INDIVIDUAL features mapped to origins -> assignment. Op: empirical reference -> match_to_reference; model reference -> overlay_model_on_data.
OBS/signal/reference_match.example: Doped XRD patterns reproduce the undoped reflections, no extra peaks

OBS/signal/feature_assignment.definition: Individual features assigned to origins: reflections indexed to phases, bands to groups, NMR signals to sites, DTG/DSC steps to processes, superposed patterns read for orientation relationship (attrs.aspect = orientation_relationship).
OBS/signal/feature_assignment.rule: vs feature_presence: indexing a set of features -> assignment; the appearance/absence of ONE specific expected feature across samples -> presence.
OBS/signal/feature_assignment.example: Six 1H NMR signals a-f mapped onto sites of the drawn polyol structure

OBS/signal/feature_presence.definition: A feature appears or disappears between samples, stages or times, or a specific expected feature is absent (qualitative yes/no).
OBS/signal/feature_presence.rule: vs feature_quantification: complete appearance/disappearance or a yes/no reading -> presence; any partial change or a residual/degree that is argued -> quantification.
OBS/signal/feature_presence.example: NCO band at 2257 cm-1 absent after urethane formation

OBS/signal/feature_shift.definition: A feature's position read relative to a reference: moving across a series (aspect=shift), or offset/overlapping with a feature of another species on the same axis, also across figures sharing that axis (aspect=overlap).
OBS/signal/feature_shift.rule: vs feature_quantification: POSITION -> shift; intensity/area/width -> quantification.
OBS/signal/feature_shift.example: (0 0 10) reflection shifts to higher 2theta with Cr content

OBS/signal/feature_quantification.definition: Feature intensity, area or width read as a measure of an amount or degree, qualitatively (grows, fades) or as a number: phase fraction, conversion, concentration, crystallite size, texture strength.
OBS/signal/feature_quantification.rule: vs presence: see presence. vs OBS/response/trend: read from the raw pattern/pole figure -> signal; read from a plotted quantity-vs-variable -> response (derives edge from the pattern node if both exist).
OBS/signal/feature_quantification.example: Integrated difference-pattern intensities give 26 +/- 5% beta phase

OBS/response.definition: A quantity read as a function of a variable or condition, over an ensemble, or split into contributions.

OBS/response/trend.definition: How a quantity changes with a varied variable or ranks across groups: direction, monotonicity, ranking (attrs.aspect=ranking for categorical groups), saturation; 2-D contours of a single response over two variables (attrs.dimension=2D).
OBS/response/trend.rule: vs characteristic_value: a direction or ranking across >=2 conditions is ARGUED -> trend; named levels are read (onset, Ecorr, value at a condition) -> characteristic_value.
OBS/response/trend.example: Yield strength rises monotonically with SiCp content

OBS/response/characteristic_value.definition: A defined point or level read from a curve, test or table: onset, peak, step, minimum, crossing that fixes a transition, value at a condition, standard-test rating, single summary statistic.
OBS/response/characteristic_value.rule: vs trend: see trend. vs distribution: a single statistic whose spread is not argued -> characteristic_value.
OBS/response/characteristic_value.example: Pencil hardness 4H; alpha-beta enthalpy crossing at 80 GPa

OBS/response/fitted_parameter.definition: A parameter obtained by fitting a functional form or model to data: exponent, slope, activation energy, rate constant, circuit element.
OBS/response/fitted_parameter.rule: vs characteristic_value: needs a functional form fitted over a range (op fit_model); a point read off the curve is characteristic_value.
OBS/response/fitted_parameter.example: Apparent stress exponent n = 7.2-8.9 from log-log creep rate vs stress

OBS/response/distribution.definition: The spread and shape of a non-imaged quantity over an ensemble (computed sites, specimens, DLS classes, indents) read as the result: range, width, tails, multimodality, overlap.
OBS/response/distribution.rule: vs characteristic_value: the SPREAD is argued -> distribution. vs OBS/morphology/feature_metric: statistics of imaged features -> feature_metric.
OBS/response/distribution.example: Vacancy formation energies over all SQS sites span 2.45-3.94 eV

OBS/response/component_partition.definition: A total response shown with its separated contributions (co-plotted or decomposed, at one condition or across conditions) so the dominant term can be read. Next: PRP/value (aspect=partition) or MEC.
OBS/response/component_partition.rule: vs trend: no variable needs to vary; if the claim is WHICH TERM DOMINATES -> component_partition; how the total changes with a variable -> trend.
OBS/response/component_partition.example: Capacitive vs diffusion-controlled share of one CV at 1 mV/s

OBS/response/regime_map.definition: Boundaries between states or regimes in a condition space, 2-D or 1-D: TTT/CCT, phase or exchange-pathway diagram, deformation-mechanism map, stability, bistability or hysteresis window. Read for WHICH STATE exists at a condition.
OBS/response/regime_map.rule: vs trend: a single response's contours over two variables is trend (dimension=2D); boundaries between qualitatively different states is regime_map.
OBS/response/regime_map.example: High- and low-amplitude branches coexist between ~12 and 25 Hz

OBS/morphology.definition: Spatial/visual content of an image or map (micrograph, photograph, element map, tomogram, fluorescence image).

OBS/morphology/appearance.definition: Qualitative reading of what imaged features look like, or whether a signal is there: shape, surface/fracture features, interface sharpness, defects, colour, gloss, film uniformity. attrs.object.
OBS/morphology/appearance.rule: vs distribution: WHAT it looks like / WHETHER a labelled signal is present -> appearance; WHERE features or a labelled species are across the field -> distribution. vs feature_metric: a number read -> feature_metric.
OBS/morphology/appearance.example: Fracture surface shows dimples and tear ridges

OBS/morphology/feature_metric.definition: A measured metric of imaged features: size or size distribution, number density, thickness, area fraction, porosity, fringe spacing, boundary fractions (also as a histogram of image-derived values).
OBS/morphology/feature_metric.rule: vs appearance: see appearance. vs OBS/response/distribution: see distribution.

OBS/morphology/distribution.definition: Spatial arrangement of features, elements or a labelled species across the field: uniformity, clustering, alignment, segregation, gradients, localisation (fluorescence, IVIS, colocalisation).
OBS/morphology/distribution.example: Dark SiC particles spread across the matrix with local clustering

STR.definition: Stage 4, structure: a claim about the material's structure at any scale, inferred from observations (or imposed by model construction).

STR/phase.definition: Crystal/phase-level structure: which phases, how much, cell dimensions, site occupancy.

STR/phase/identity.definition: Which phases or crystal structures are present, incl. 'no secondary phase' and mesoscale periodic arrangements (attrs.scale=mesoscale). Requires structure-sensitive evidence (diffraction, spectroscopy of structure).
STR/phase/identity.rule: vs STR/chemistry/composition: a phase named only from stoichiometry (EDS Ca:P) is composition with attrs.phase_named_from=stoichiometry. vs fraction: WHICH vs HOW MUCH.

STR/phase/fraction.definition: How much of a crystalline phase is present, incl. its evolution: phase fraction, degree of transformation, polymer crystallinity. A proxy is named in attrs.proxy.
STR/phase/fraction.rule: vs identity: see identity. vs STR/chemistry/composition: amount of a CRYSTALLINE phase -> fraction; loss or gain of an amorphous/organic constituent or element content -> composition (attrs.scope).
STR/phase/fraction.example: Transformation completes in 200-300 ns near Tm

STR/phase/lattice.definition: Unit-cell dimensions, interlayer spacing or lattice strain and their change.
STR/phase/lattice.rule: vs site_occupancy: HOW BIG the cell is -> lattice; WHO sits where -> site_occupancy.
STR/phase/lattice.example: Layer spacing c shrinks linearly from 16.97 to 16.68 A with Cr

STR/phase/site_occupancy.definition: Distribution of constituents over the crystallographic sites of a phase: site preference, inversion, antisites, sublattice order/disorder (attrs.aspect = preference | ordering).
STR/phase/site_occupancy.rule: vs STR/defect/point: which-site/ordering claims WITHOUT a charge, carrier or diffusion argument -> site_occupancy; with one -> defect/point.
STR/phase/site_occupancy.example: Fe3+ takes octahedral sites, confining Co2+ to tetrahedral sites

STR/chemistry.definition: Molecular/chemical-level structure: bonds and configuration, elemental composition and valence.

STR/chemistry/bonding.definition: Bonds, functional groups, linkages or coordination present or converted, up to full molecular structure; configuration/conformation (aspect=configuration); noncovalent intermolecular packing: pi-stacking, J/H-aggregation, host-guest, charge-transfer cocrystals (aspect=intermolecular_packing).
STR/chemistry/bonding.rule: vs composition: HOW atoms are bonded or packed -> bonding; WHAT elements/valences are present -> composition.
STR/chemistry/bonding.example: Oil double bonds converted to oxirane rings; J-aggregation of ICG

STR/chemistry/composition.definition: WHAT a phase or region is made of: elemental composition, stoichiometry, valence, solute content, per-layer composition, loss/gain of an amorphous or organic constituent (attrs.scope), phases named only from stoichiometry.
STR/chemistry/composition.rule: vs STR/microstructure/distribution: WHAT -> composition; WHERE -> distribution. vs phase/fraction and phase/identity: see those.
STR/chemistry/composition.example: Reaction layer II is Co/Ni-rich Al(Co,Ni)2Ti

STR/defect/point.definition: Substitutional, interstitial or vacancy species by charge state, compensation, position (aspect=position) or concentration (aspect=concentration); drives carrier, ionic, diffusion arguments. May be imposed by model construction (basis=imposed).
STR/defect/point.rule: vs site_occupancy: see site_occupancy. vs PRP/descriptor: a defect CONCENTRATION is defect/point; carrier density, mobility, m*, diffusivity are descriptor.
STR/defect/point.example: Cr3+ substitutes Ti4+ as an acceptor-type defect

STR/defect/extended.definition: Line and planar defects (dislocations, stacking faults, twins, APBs) and their density; drives mechanical and phonon arguments.
STR/defect/extended.rule: vs point: dimensionality. vs microstructure/damage: crystallographic defects vs loss of continuity (cracks, voids).
STR/defect/extended.example: Higher Cr levels remove planar stacking faults

STR/microstructure.definition: Arrangement of grains, particles, pores, phases and cracks at meso/micro scale.

STR/microstructure/feature_size.definition: Size of structural units (grains, particles, crystallites, pores, layers); refine/coarsen as attrs.direction.
STR/microstructure/feature_size.rule: vs shape: HOW BIG -> feature_size; WHAT FORM -> shape.
STR/microstructure/feature_size.example: Matrix grains refined from 65 to 22 um

STR/microstructure/distribution.definition: Spatial distribution of a constituent: dispersion, agglomeration, segregation, gradient, shell/coating coverage (aspect=coverage) and filler-network contact/connectivity (aspect=connectivity).
STR/microstructure/distribution.rule: vs shape: coverage/where a constituent lies -> distribution; the geometry of a built unit (core-shell, sheath, hollow) -> shape. vs porosity: when the argued quantity is the void, porosity; when it is where the constituent is, distribution. vs STR/interface: contact STATE (bonding, charge transfer) across the boundary -> interface.
STR/microstructure/distribution.example: Near-uniform SiCp distribution with few agglomerates; CNT network fully covers the fibre

STR/microstructure/shape.definition: Shape and topography of structural units or of a built architecture (lenticular, equiaxed, lamellar, core-shell, hollow single-cavity, strut network, facets, roughness).
STR/microstructure/shape.rule: vs distribution: see distribution. vs porosity: a single designed cavity or shell -> shape; pore volume fraction, SSA or connectivity -> porosity.
STR/microstructure/shape.example: Lens-shaped beta grains, about one nucleus per alpha grain

STR/microstructure/porosity.definition: Amount, connectivity and hierarchy of porosity: void fraction, relative density, open vs closed, interconnection, network mesh, processing voids, specific surface area. Next: transport/ingrowth or correction of property values.
STR/microstructure/porosity.rule: vs feature_size: pore SIZE -> feature_size. vs damage: load/environment-induced voids -> damage. vs shape: see shape.
STR/microstructure/porosity.example: Ceramics remain 20-29% porous after 1500 C sintering

STR/microstructure/orientation.definition: Orientation state: crystallographic texture, molecular/fibre orientation, grain-boundary character (misorientation distribution, LAGB/HAGB/twin fractions).
STR/microstructure/orientation.rule: vs feature_size/shape: an orientation claim licenses anisotropy/slip/recrystallisation inferences; size and shape claims do not.
STR/microstructure/orientation.example: Electropulsing weakens the basal texture and raises the HAGB fraction

STR/microstructure/damage.definition: Loss of continuity induced in a made material by load, thermal cycling or environment: microcracks, gouge, delamination, fibre fracture, degradation-opened cracks, binder dissolution that de-bonds grains (aspect=binder_dissolution).
STR/microstructure/damage.rule: vs porosity: designed or processing pores -> porosity. vs defect/extended: see extended.
STR/microstructure/damage.example: Gouge of loose debris flanked by comb cracks, damage zone 2-3 grains wide

STR/interface.definition: State of an interface or boundary between constituents or with a substrate: bonding, reaction layer, coherency/orientation relationship, wetting, adhesion, contact enabling charge transfer.

PRP.definition: Stage 5, property: a claim about a property of the material or of an assembly (attrs.object); attrs.property_family required; attrs.basis=argued when unmeasured.

PRP/value.definition: The level of a property or its change with a design variable or condition, incl. a claim that one contribution dominates the total (attrs.aspect = partition). Quantity, direction and family in attrs.
PRP/value.rule: vs PRF/*: argued from structure or ranked against the design variable -> value; judged at a use condition, against an external criterion, or as a composite metric -> PRF. vs diagnostic: see diagnostic.
PRP/value.example: Tensile yield strength increases with SiCp; reduction of kappa is dominated by the electronic part (aspect=partition)

PRP/behavior_class.definition: A categorical classification of how the material behaves: failure/wear/decay mode, conduction type, magnetic order, pairing symmetry, kinematic behaviour of an architected cell.
PRP/behavior_class.rule: vs value: a CATEGORY, not a level. vs PRF/service_capability: how it fails -> behavior_class; ranking or pass under a (simulated) service condition -> service_capability.
PRP/behavior_class.example: Mixed ductile-brittle fracture, brittle fraction growing with SiCp

PRP/descriptor.definition: A microscopic descriptor between structure and a measured property as intermediate cause: carrier density, mobility, effective mass, diffusivity.
PRP/descriptor.rule: vs STR/defect/point: defect concentration is STR. vs value: descriptor is not itself the measured headline property; it explains one.
PRP/descriptor.example: Effective mass increases with Cr, adding to the Seebeck gain

PRP/diagnostic.definition: A quantity whose role is to identify a mechanism via a known mapping (stress exponent, activation energy, Avrami exponent, Tafel slope, b-value, 2Delta/kTc). Next: KNW/lookup -> MEC/identification.
PRP/diagnostic.rule: vs value: the same quantity is diagnostic ONLY if a KNW/lookup or KNW/model -> MEC/identification follows; used as a level or ranking it is value.

PRF.definition: Stage 6, performance: a claim about how the material, device or process performs in a use or test condition.

PRF/figure_of_merit.definition: A composite application metric combining several properties or normalising a property per mass, volume or cost in the field's ranking convention (ZT, energy density at a power density, specific strength, specific capacitance at a stated rate).
PRF/figure_of_merit.rule: vs qualification: no external pass/fail threshold -> FOM. vs PRP/value: argued from structure as a trend -> value; used to rank devices/materials against others -> FOM.
PRF/figure_of_merit.example: ZT at 750 K rises from 0.24 to 0.29

PRF/service_capability.definition: The material, device or method performs (or fails) under a stated use condition, or a built prototype or process demonstrably does the job; includes in-vivo endpoints and endpoint-quality tissue markers.
PRF/service_capability.rule: vs qualification: no external criterion applied. vs MEC/pathway: host biomarkers and biodistribution invoked to EXPLAIN an endpoint are MEC/pathway.
PRF/service_capability.example: Improved creep resistance at 175 C and 80-120 MPa for >=15 wt% SiCp

PRF/qualification.definition: Performance judged against an external criterion: standard pass/fail, spec, rating compared with a threshold, or a community benchmark condition (overpotential at 10 mA/cm2).
PRF/qualification.rule: vs FOM and PRP/value: only when a threshold, spec or benchmark condition is applied; a standard rating ranked against formulation is PRP/value.
PRF/qualification.example: Coatings meet hardness, gloss, adhesion and chemical-resistance requirements

MEC.definition: Bridge: a mechanistic explanation linking cause to effect across stages; attrs.mechanism_class names the physics.

MEC/pathway.definition: A causal pathway by which a cause produces an effect; incl. explanatory host biomarkers and in-vivo biodistribution (mechanism_class=pharmacokinetic). attrs.basis = evidenced | argued | attributed.
MEC/pathway.rule: vs identification: a pathway BUILT from evidence -> pathway; one member PICKED from a known catalogue -> identification.
MEC/pathway.example: SiC particles act as heterogeneous nucleation sites and restrict grain growth

MEC/identification.definition: The operative mechanism is identified as one member of a known catalogue (rate-controlling step, transformation mode, scattering regime), via a diagnostic and a lookup or via an experiment that isolates one candidate (decoupling, selective suppression).
MEC/identification.example: Creep is climb-controlled; texture change is driven by grain growth, not recrystallisation

MEC/tradeoff.definition: A net outcome explained by one contribution outweighing an opposing one; carries counteracts edges.
MEC/tradeoff.rule: vs pathway: needs two opposing contributions and a counteracts edge.
MEC/tradeoff.example: Lower total thermal conductivity outweighs the power-factor loss, so ZT rises

KNW.definition: Premise: prior knowledge, literature or theory brought in as an input; never spine.

KNW/precedent.definition: A specific earlier result (own or others') used as analogy, support or comparator.
KNW/precedent.rule: vs fact: a RESULT of a study -> precedent; a tabulated constant or known structure -> fact.
KNW/precedent.example: Isothermal martensite in Fe-Ni shows S-shaped autocatalytic kinetics

KNW/model.definition: A named model, formalism or governing equation used to compute, fit or predict.
KNW/model.rule: vs lookup: an equation to compute with -> model; a mapping from a value/feature to its meaning -> lookup.

KNW/lookup.definition: A known mapping from an observable value or feature to its interpretation: diagnostic value -> mechanism, band position -> group, reference card.
KNW/lookup.example: n ~ 5 indicates lattice-diffusion-controlled climb; 1730 cm-1 is urethane C=O

KNW/fact.definition: A tabulated fact or known structure of a constituent used as a premise (constant, radius, composition, crystal-structure model).

DSC.definition: Stage 7, discussion: conclusion, comparison, guidance, limitation or outlook drawn from the results.

DSC/conclusion.definition: Summary claim of what was shown and what is new; the spine terminus.
DSC/conclusion.rule: vs design_guidance: what WAS shown -> conclusion; what to DO -> guidance.
DSC/conclusion.example: Cr doping optimises carrier concentration and, unlike other acceptors, raises m*

DSC/comparison.definition: Results set against prior work, a model prediction or an incumbent; attrs.against = prior_work | model | baseline, attrs.verdict.
DSC/comparison.rule: vs KNW/precedent: the precedent is the input; the comparison is the verdict drawn in this paper.
DSC/comparison.example: Models agree above 1400 K but overestimate Ea by 50% at 1200 K

DSC/design_guidance.definition: A generalised design rule, optimum window or trade-off recommendation drawn from the results.
DSC/design_guidance.rule: vs conclusion: see conclusion. vs outlook: guidance is backed by this paper's results; outlook is proposed next work.
DSC/design_guidance.example: <=10 wt% SiCp suffices for strength; creep benefit needs >=15 wt%

DSC/limitation.definition: A stated limit of method or data, or an anomaly attributed to artefact, that bounds a claim (kind = method | anomaly | scope).
DSC/limitation.rule: vs OBS audit nodes: the limitation is the paper's (or annotator's) stated bound; the readout that reveals it is an OBS with a qualifies edge.
DSC/limitation.example: beta < 10% undetectable; the 1575 K outlier attributed to laser misalignment

DSC/outlook.definition: Proposed application or next experiment (kind = application | research).
DSC/outlook.example: Suitable for floor-care and decorative coatings

rels.motivates: HYP/DSC/OBS gives reason for a DES/PRC choice or a test; a weighed claim (PRP/PRF/MEC, e.g. a trade-off or ranking) may motivate a DES/down_select (screen-then-choose)
rels.realizes: a DES choice is carried out by a PRC act or a measurement; in computation-first papers also by constructing an in-silico structure, in which case dst may be a STR node with attrs.basis=imposed; a spine DES/method whose measurement is a headline contribution may realize the STR/PRP/MEC claim it makes measurable
rels.feeds_into: src PRC act's product is the workpiece, precursor, mold or template of dst PRC act (ordered multi-step route). PRC->PRC only; replaces realizes/premise_for between PRC nodes
rels.produces: a PRC act or condition yields a structural state
rels.evidences: an OBS supports a claim (STR/PRP/PRF/MEC) or a DSC/comparison or DSC/limitation verdict. Source must be OBS
rels.causes: physical causation in the material: one state leads to another (processing -> structure -> property -> performance). Not for claim-to-conclusion reasoning
rels.explains: a MEC accounts for a claim
rels.premise_for: a KNW node, or an in-paper node used as an input, supplies an assumption, equation, parameter or condition value for another inference or derivation (absorbs proposed 'parameterizes')
rels.contrasts: a claim or OBS is compared against a control, baseline, model or alternative
rels.rules_out: evidence or reasoning rejects an alternative explanation
rels.derives: dst OBS is computed from src OBS by arithmetic, data reduction, fitting or re-plotting; dst is NOT independent evidence (absorbs proposed 'reduces_to'). Carries an mm_op when src has a figure
rels.qualifies: a limitation, caveat, anomaly or contradicting readout bounds the scope or confidence of a claim, or contradicts it outright; the strength of the conflict is carried by the target's image_support (partial | contradicts) and the audit node's label
rels.counteracts: src effect opposes the outcome dst stands for (the loss term of a trade-off)
rels.supports: a claim is used as a premise for another claim or conclusion (claim -> claim or claim -> DSC reasoning), as opposed to physical causation (causes) or direct measurement (evidences)

modality_notes.diffraction_pattern: Intensity vs scattering angle/vector, 1D (XRD trace, radial profile) or 2D (SAED, detector image)
modality_notes.spectrum: Intensity vs energy/wavenumber/shift/binding energy (IR, Raman, XPS, NMR, UV-vis, EDS spectrum, XAS), and real-space radial functions (FT-EXAFS, PDF); computed DOS/pDOS/COOP curves
modality_notes.xy_curve: Any quantitative plot of a quantity vs a variable or category: line, scatter, bar/histogram (incl. histograms of image-derived values), log-log, contour of a response. Not for 1D diffraction traces, spectra, line scans or dispersion diagrams
modality_notes.spatial_map: Map of a quantity or element over sample space in 2D (EDS/EBSD/EPMA map, strain map, tomogram slice, property map of hardness/modulus/conductivity) or 1D (EDS/EPMA line scan vs distance, intensity line profile across an image)
modality_notes.photograph: Macroscopic camera image of samples or devices
modality_notes.schematic: Drawn diagram, reaction scheme or structure model
modality_notes.simulation_render: Rendered simulation output (atomistic snapshot, FEM field)
modality_notes.text_only: Readout stated in text with no figure in the packet
modality_notes.composite_rule: For multi-panel figures use the modality of the panel actually read; if a node reads two panel kinds, split the node
modality_notes.volume_render: 3D surface or volume rendering of experimental tomographic or serial-section data (micro-CT, FIB-SEM, electron tomography, atom-probe reconstruction), often cut away or colour-segmented; segmentation/smoothing artefacts apply. Simulated 3D output stays simulation_render
modality_notes.orientation_distribution: Intensity over orientation space, not physical space: pole figures, inverse-pole-figure density plots, ODF sections. An EBSD IPF-coloured map is spatial_map
modality_notes.dispersion_diagram: Energy or frequency vs wavevector along a high-symmetry path: electronic band structure, phonon or magnon dispersion. The DOS panel beside it is spectrum. Kept with 1 paper of 60 because band-structure and phonon-dispersion plots are standard in computational papers of every material class

values.measured: directly recorded by an instrument or test
values.derived: computed in this paper from other OBS (must have an incoming derives edge)
values.computed: output of simulation, theory or model calculation (DFT, FEM, CALPHAD, analytic model)

provenance.note: Review papers: an OBS reproduced from a cited study keeps the source's provenance and adds attrs.reproduced_from=[ref].

values.shown: the figure visibly shows the claim as stated
values.partial: the figure supports a weaker, qualified or subset version (some panels/samples, within noise, low magnification)
values.not_shown: the figure does not resolve the claimed feature; the claim rests on text or tables
values.contradicts: the figure shows something inconsistent with the stated claim

image_support.note: Record what the image shows instead in attrs.image_note. Things the figure shows that the text never states become their own OBS node with attrs.text_silent=true. An audit OBS node whose label states the discrepancy itself has image_support=shown (the figure shows the discrepancy); the conflict is carried by its qualifies/contrasts edge. From v04: fill image_support only after opening the image; nodes whose figure was not opened carry figs=[] and attrs.fig_ref (the figure id), never an image_support judged from the caption. Figure ids follow the image file, not the caption.

values.true: node lies on the paper's primary line of argument (HYP -> DES -> PRC -> STR -> PRP -> PRF -> DSC/conclusion, with bridging MEC)
values.false: evidence, premise, audit or side branch

spine.note: See PROTOCOL.md 'Spine and periphery'. OBS and KNW nodes are never spine; 10-20 spine nodes per paper. From v03: at most two parallel branches plus one control branch that ends in a PRP/STR linked by contrasts to the main branch; DES/method may be spine when the method is a headline contribution (link by realizes to the claim it makes measurable); DES/down_select is reached by motivates from the weighed claim. From v04: in method/tool papers a PRP of the tool-workpiece assembly (attrs.object=assembly) may sit upstream of the STR it produces (PRC -causes-> PRP -supports-> MEC -explains-> STR).

basis.applies_to: attrs.basis on STR/PRP/PRF/MEC claims (optional; default evidenced)

values.evidenced: supported by incoming evidences edges in this paper
values.argued: reasoned from other claims or literature, no direct measurement (e.g. dislocation density inferred from incomplete DRX)
values.attributed: asserted cause without a pathway or evidence
values.imposed: set by model construction in a computation (e.g. substitutional N placed in a DFT cell)

basis.note: Evidence through a proxy (KAM for transformed fraction, colour for dose) is still evidenced; name the proxy in attrs.proxy

values.true: the figure shows content the text never states AND it bears on a spine claim (qualifies, contradicts or would change it)

text_silent.note: Otherwise record the content in attrs.image_note of the nearest OBS node. Numbers in labels are read from the figure; the text value goes in image_note.

modality.values: see modalities and modality_notes; split a node that reads two panel kinds

mm_op_families.read: Extract a feature from one figure: a direction, a point, a spread, a local feature or a spatial pattern.
mm_op_families.compare: Set two or more traces, panels, figures or sources against each other and read the difference, co-variation or coincidence.
mm_op_families.match: Map figure content to a reference, a design, a label or a known class.
mm_op_families.quantify: Turn figure content into numbers, parameters or a new derived series (the ops allowed on derives edges, plus register_colocated_views for two-channel ratios).
mm_op_families.check: Test agreement or consistency: model against data, curves under normalisation, figures against each other or against the text.

read_trend.definition: Read the direction, monotonicity, saturation or change of ranking of a quantity across an ordered series or along an axis.
read_trend.rule: vs read_characteristic_point: if a crossing or point yields a VALUE (transition pressure, onset) use read_characteristic_point; read_trend only for direction or ranking.

read_characteristic_point.definition: Read a defined point from a curve or scan: onset, peak, minimum, inflection/step, threshold or curve crossing, value at a condition; also locating a sample relative to regime boundaries.

read_distribution_statistics.definition: Read range, central value, width, tails, per-class offsets or overlap from a distribution of a non-imaged quantity. Failure modes: few counts, binning, colour classes, intensity vs number weighting.
read_distribution_statistics.rule: vs measure_feature_metric: image-derived histograms go to measure_feature_metric.

inspect_local_feature.definition: Judge a local feature (interface, defect, grain shape) in one high-magnification view; representativeness is an assumption.
inspect_local_feature.rule: vs assess_spatial_distribution: ONE feature in one view vs arrangement ACROSS a field.

assess_spatial_distribution.definition: Judge uniformity, clustering, alignment, segregation or localisation of features, elements or a labelled species across a field or map.

compare_across_conditions.definition: Compare panels, frames, traces or curves that differ in one condition (design variable, stage, time, before/after) and read the difference, incl. following a spectral or diffraction feature through a stack of traces.
compare_across_conditions.rule: vs track_feature_across_series: use track only when the IDENTITY of an object through frames is what the inference needs.

track_feature_across_series.definition: Follow one identified OBJECT (atom, particle, layer, crack tip, domain wall, ion) through time-lapse, trajectory or loading frames and read its displacement, sequence or appearance. Failure modes: object identity between frames, frame-interval aliasing (sequential vs simultaneous events).
track_feature_across_series.rule: vs compare_across_conditions: a peak followed through stacked traces is compare_across_conditions (the OBS type already says a feature moved).

compare_coplotted_quantities.definition: Read two or more different quantities, species or components on shared axes (or in separate figures sharing axis quantity and units) and judge dominance or positional overlap (aspect=overlap). Audit: bandwidths, same medium/state, same scale; a non-overlap is also a result.
compare_coplotted_quantities.rule: vs correlate_across_series: coplotted = different quantities on ONE axis; correlate = same sample series across DIFFERENT ordinates.

compare_with_reference_value.definition: Position this work's data against reference VALUES plotted, tabulated or quoted alongside: prior work, incumbents, constants, an in-paper benchmark system.
compare_with_reference_value.rule: vs match_to_reference: reference values (points) -> this op; a reference TRACE judged for coincidence -> match_to_reference.

correlate_across_series.definition: Align the same sample series across two or more figures with different ordinates and judge co-variation; licenses correlational attribution only.

register_colocated_views.definition: Register two or more views of the SAME region (image + map, line scan, point analysis, SAED at marked positions, magnifications, probe/indent positions on a photograph) so content read in one is located on a feature in the other; allowed on derives edges when a colocalisation coefficient or channel ratio is computed. Failure modes: misregistration, probe size, bleed-through, thresholds.
register_colocated_views.rule: vs compare_across_conditions: same region, different channels; not different conditions.

match_to_reference.definition: Judge a whole trace or image against an EMPIRICAL reference (parent sample, standard, database card).
match_to_reference.rule: vs overlay_model_on_data: a model, fit or simulation reference goes to overlay_model_on_data.

match_to_design.definition: Compare an image of a fabricated object with its intended geometry (CAD/STL, mold, template, target dimension) and judge fidelity.
match_to_design.rule: vs match_to_reference: the reference is the design intent, not a measured or model trace.

assign_features.definition: Assign individual peaks, bands, signals, steps or contrast levels to phases, groups, sites or processes via a known mapping; incl. orientation relationship in superposed patterns (aspect=orientation_relationship).
assign_features.rule: vs recognize_signature: individual features -> assign; a whole shape -> recognize_signature.

recognize_signature.definition: Match a visible morphology or a curve shape to a known class that implies a mechanism (dimples -> ductile; lenticular -> martensitic; sigmoid, C-curve).

measure_feature_metric.definition: Measure sizes, counts, densities, thicknesses, area or boundary fractions of imaged features, or extract a line profile from one image.
measure_feature_metric.rule: vs convert_to_quantity: measuring geometry in the image -> this op; converting a signal through a relation -> convert_to_quantity.

convert_to_quantity.definition: Convert a feature or readout into a physical quantity through a stated relation; attrs.via = intensity (peak/ROI integrals -> amount; audit background, saturation) | position (Bragg, Vegard; audit reference and calibration of axis) | calibration (in-paper calibration; audit target inside calibrated range, comparable state, monotone inversion) | known_relation (C = I dt/dV, Arrhenius from two points) | model (Rothwarf-Taylor inversion).
convert_to_quantity.rule: vs fit_model: a relation applied to given points -> convert; parameters obtained by fitting a form over a range -> fit_model.

fit_model.definition: Fit a functional form to data to obtain parameters: slope/intercept on linearised axes, power law, Arrhenius, Tauc, equivalent circuit, deconvolution; attrs.form = linearised | power_law | nonlinear | circuit | decomposition. Audit: fitted window, constraints, number of points.

replot_derived_series.definition: Build a new series or diagram from other readouts: arithmetic combination, subtraction of a background/reference trace, aggregation, resampling at iso-levels, re-plot against another variable.
replot_derived_series.rule: vs collapse_by_normalization: if the re-plot is made to TEST whether curves merge, use collapse_by_normalization on the evidences edge.

overlay_model_on_data.definition: Judge agreement region by region between model/fit/simulation output and data, overlaid, side by side or in matched panels. Audit: a parameter tuned on the same data makes agreement circular.

collapse_by_normalization.definition: Re-plot against a normalised or corrected variable and check whether curves or points from different conditions merge; the merge is the evidence. Audit: high-leverage points.

cross_check_consistency.definition: Verify that quantities read from different figures, panels or the text agree arithmetically or in trend; incl. flagging a point or series that deviates and setting it aside (aspect=outlier).
cross_check_consistency.rule: vs overlay_model_on_data: data vs data or data vs text; model vs data is overlay.

conditional_renames.when: src node type is OBS/signal/* (a feature followed through stacked traces)
identity of an imaged/simulated object through frames licenses the inference (r03 ruling #9 edges adfm.201901327 o20->s8, aenm.201902373 o26->e6)
the reference is model, fit or simulation output (nmat2713 b23, nl201541y a21, s41563-024-01862-8 d12)

property_family_notes.catalytic: activity/selectivity of a catalyst: electro-, photo-, thermocatalytic (OER overpotential, dye-degradation rate)
property_family_notes.thermodynamic: formation, binding, cohesive, surface or interfacial energies and phase stability
property_family_notes.ionic_electrochemical: ionic conduction, redox capacity, battery/supercapacitor behaviour; not catalytic activity
property_family_notes.chemical_corrosion: corrosion, oxidation, chemical resistance, degradation in environment, including hydrolytic, enzymatic and in-body biodegradation (Mg implant corrosion, polymer hydrolysis, scaffold mass loss)
property_family_notes.biological: in-vitro response of cells, bacteria or proteins to the material (viability, adhesion, proliferation, antibacterial activity, haemolysis); in-vivo endpoints are PRF/service_capability
property_family_notes.photochemical: light-triggered generation or release of species by the material (photosensitised ROS, NO release, photo-uncaging); not turnover catalysis
property_family_notes.surface: wetting, adhesion, friction coefficient and wear rate (tribology); a wear-mode classification is PRP/behavior_class

changelog: FINAL (merge phase). Types 82 -> 81 entries (10 L1 + 7 L2 + 64 leaves); mm_ops 27 -> 22; mm_op families 6 -> 5; rels 14 (qualifies redefined); modalities 13 (unchanged).

Merged mm_ops: quantify_from_intensity + quantify_from_position + convert_via_calibration -> convert_to_quantity (attrs.via); extract_slope -> fit_model (attrs.form); flag_outlier -> cross_check_consistency (aspect=outlier); subtract_reference -> replot_derived_series.

Narrowed: track_feature_across_series to object identity through frames (stacked-trace uses -> compare_across_conditions); match_to_reference to empirical references (model references -> overlay_model_on_data, which now covers side-by-side panels). Family transform folded into quantify.

Kept against merge proposals: OBS/response/component_partition (single-condition decompositions have no varied variable), OBS/response/regime_map (3 papers; incl. 1-D state windows), PRP/diagnostic (diagnostic chain in 7 papers), collapse_by_normalization (3 papers), PRF/figure_of_merit vs PRF/qualification (sharpened).
Every leaf and mm_op now carries a decision rule vs its nearest sibling and usage over 60 papers; L1 and L2 entries carry one-line definitions and a level field.

Boundary broadenings: bonding (+intermolecular packing), MEC/pathway (+biodistribution), MEC/identification (+decoupling experiments), DES/route (+purpose=decouple), DES/base_system (whole-molecule designs), PRC/deposition (+conversion coatings), PRC/treatment and PRC/stimulus (in-silico pressure), PRC/stimulus usage note, microstructure/distribution (+coverage, connectivity), damage (+binder dissolution), STR/defect/point (+concentration; removed from PRP/descriptor), OBS/signal/reference_match (+response curves vs model), compare_coplotted_quantities (+cross-figure), register_colocated_views (+allowed on derives), convert_to_quantity via=intensity (+image ROI).

Node-field rules: image_support only from opened images (figs=[] + attrs.fig_ref otherwise); review provenance attrs.reproduced_from; spine allows PRP(object=assembly) upstream of STR in tool papers; text_silent documented as a node field.

usage.scope: r01-r04 graphs (60 papers, 2109 nodes, 2625 edges) after v01-v04 renames and v04 conditional_renames; [count, papers]
